problem: The P-1 evidence policy contained two bootstrap blockers: exact-head visual provenance required a commit to contain its own final SHA, and technical bootstrap collections/scripts could be classified as player-facing solely by resource extension. BB-001 could not satisfy those constraints without weakening or bypassing governance.

decision.rationale: Use a literal $PR_HEAD binding whose concrete value is supplied and retained by exact-head CI, and give explicitly high-risk technical prefixes/files precedence over generic player-facing extension classification. This preserves exact-head evidence and strong technical manifests while making bootstrap PRs satisfiable.

research.candidate_pool_exception: Shipped-game reference research is not applicable to repository evidence-policy correctness.
research.reference_exception: This is a CI/Git data-model problem rather than player-facing design.

anti_pattern.observation: Git object IDs are hashes of object contents; changing committed manifest content changes the resulting object graph and commit identity.
anti_pattern.lesson: Do not require a committed file to contain the final commit ID that depends on that file.

official_docs.verified_constraint: GitHub Actions exposes event and SHA context data to workflow steps, allowing trusted CI to bind evidence to the concrete pull-request head at execution time.
Git objects are immutable and identified by cryptographic hashes of their type and contents, so a commit cannot stably embed its own not-yet-created final object ID as ordinary tracked content.

alternatives.reason: Keeps exact-head provenance and high-risk technical evidence while making both checks mechanically satisfiable.

governance.trust_boundary_change: The trust boundary remains trusted-base policy. Exact-head identity is represented declaratively as $PR_HEAD in committed manifests and resolved by trusted CI; explicitly technical app/ and other high-risk prefixes/files take precedence over generic presentation-extension classification.
governance.bypass_analysis: Arbitrary SHA strings remain rejected for player-facing provenance. UI/gameplay/main paths remain player-facing. process/trivial still cannot classify meaningful runtime. The runtime evidence workflow remains read-only and exact-head. No bypass actors, approval shortcuts or direct candidate-policy authority are introduced.
governance.rollback: Revert this PR to restore the prior classifier/provenance rules and app path filter; doing so would intentionally restore the BB-001 blockers and should only be used if a replacement satisfiable binding/classifier is introduced simultaneously.

known_limitations: The Protect main GitHub ruleset is temporarily disabled by the repository owner during repair; repository policy code cannot re-enable the external ruleset through the available connector.
